projection.growthBasis: 5-data-point geometric mean of annual nominal growth, SIPRI 2020-2025 (5 compounding years), then compounded 1 year from basedOnYear (2025) to currentYear (2026). SIPRI Trends in World Military Expenditure, 2025 was published on 2026-04-27. (2025 nominal growth decelerated to ~6.2%, so this geometric-mean extrapolation is upper-leaning).

source: SIPRI Trends in World Military Expenditure, 2025

sources.name: The Lancet Oncology Commission — Global cancer care costs
American Cancer Society — Cancer Treatment & Survivorship Facts and Figures

categories.methodology: Approximate average per-patient cost of a full first-course cancer treatment (surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy and follow-up) in a high-income setting, drawn from Lancet Oncology Commission and ACS cost-of-care estimates.

sources.name: Gates & Chambers — From Aspiration to Action: What Will It Take to End Malaria? (2015)
WHO — Global Technical Strategy for Malaria 2016–2030 (2021 update)

categories.methodology: Total additional investment to eradicate malaria (~USD 90-120B), per Gates & Chambers 2015 'From Aspiration to Action' and WHO Global Technical Strategy; WHO targets eradication by 2050.

sources.name: Laborde et al. — Ending hunger: science must stop neglecting smallholder farmers, Nature 2020

categories.methodology: Average additional annual public expenditure (approximately USD 33 billion) required from donors and low/middle-income governments through 2030 to end hunger (SDG 2), per Ceres2030 / IFPRI models published in Nature Food.

sources.name: World Bank — The Costs of Meeting the 2030 SDG Targets on Drinking Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene

categories.methodology: Annual capital investment of ~USD 37.6 billion needed through 2030 for universal safely-managed drinking water (SDG 6.1 component), per the World Bank's SDG 6 costing study (Hutton & Varughese 2016).

sources.name: UNESCO Global Education Monitoring Report — Pricing the right to education
Global Partnership for Education — Results Report

categories.methodology: Approximate per-pupil capital cost (construction plus basic equipment) of creating one new school place in a low- or lower-middle-income country, derived from UNESCO GEM Report and GPE infrastructure costings.

sources.name: Sriudomporn, Watts, Sim et al. — Achieving Immunization Agenda 2030 coverage targets for 14 pathogens: Projected product and immunization delivery costs for 194 Countries, 2021–2030 (Vaccine: X 2022)
Gavi, The Vaccine Alliance — Resource Mobilisation Process

categories.methodology: Estimated ~USD 27 billion per year — the full annual cost of delivering a routine immunisation schedule against 14 pathogens to every child across 194 countries (~USD 269.8 billion total over 2021-2030, vaccine product plus delivery), per Sriudomporn et al., 'Achieving Immunization Agenda 2030 coverage targets', Vaccine X 2022.

sources.name: Our World in Data — Total shortfall from the $3/day poverty line
World Bank — Poverty, Prosperity, and Planet 2024

categories.methodology: Annual income transfer (poverty gap) to lift everyone above the USD 3.00/day international poverty line (2021 PPP), ~USD 315 billion/year per World Bank PIP / Our World in Data.

sources.name: Rainforest Trust — Cost per acre protected
FAO — Global Forest Resources Assessment (tropical forest area)

categories.methodology: Total cost to place all of Earth's remaining tropical rainforest under durable legal protection. Computed as USD 25 per hectare (Rainforest Trust per-acre averages scaled to a hectare) multiplied by approximately 1.8 billion hectares of remaining tropical forest (FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment 2020).

sources.name: IRENA — Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2023
IEA — Renewables 2023 Analysis and Forecast to 2028

categories.methodology: Capital cost to install 1 GW of utility-scale solar PV. IRENA's 2023 global weighted-average was $758/kW, so ~$1B installs ~1.3 GW — enough to power ~300,000 European homes.
Total funding requirement of the UN-coordinated Global Humanitarian Appeal for 2024 (USD 46.4 billion to assist roughly 181 million people), as stated by UN OCHA.
